must_remember: Lissajous figures are formed by the superposition of two mutually perpendicular simple harmonic motions.
When frequencies are equal ($\omega_x = \omega_y$) and phase difference $\delta = 0$ or $\pi$, the resulting path is a straight line.
A circle is formed when amplitudes are equal ($a = b$) and the phase difference is an odd multiple of $\pi/2$.
The frequency ratio $\omega_y / \omega_x$ can be determined by counting the number of tangential intersections along the vertical and horizontal axes.
A Cathode-Ray Oscilloscope (CRO) uses sinusoidal signals applied to X and Y plates to display stationary Lissajous figures for precise frequency comparison.

glossary.meaning: The trajectory traced by a particle subjected simultaneously to two mutually perpendicular simple harmonic motions.
The difference in phase between the orthogonal simple harmonic motions along the X-axis and Y-axis.
Frequencies that are in the ratio of small integers, producing closed open loops or curves.
An electronic test instrument used to visually display and measure electrical signals and Lissajous figures.
